reason: Claim c1 is confirmed, in_scope, and backed by decisive evidence tied to the stated input domain. problem.txt (the operative contract; no test.py/get_inputs exists) requires abs(actual[i]-sin(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for EVERY finite FP16 value including extrema ±65504, with relative tolerance zero and a single verdict over the whole domain. The exhaustive sweep (t21, evidence c1.e3) tested all 12,288 finite FP16 values with |x|>=1024 and found two violations: x=+63168 and x=-63168, each with absolute error 1.0039e-6 > 1e-6 against the FP64 torch.sin reference on the exact stored FP16 values. The earlier t10 datapoint (x=-63168, err 1.0039e-6) reproduced exactly in the fresh exhaustive run, ruling out a probe artifact. The mechanism matches the kernel source: the split-constant reduction r_hi = x - q*1.5703125 is computed in FP32, where subtracting two ~|x| quantities loses precision to catastrophic cancellation. Although the margin is only 0.4% over tolerance, the contract sets a hard per-element absolute bound with no exemption for approximations ("any range reduction or polynomial is permitted only if the 1e-6 bound holds everywhere"), so any violation on any legal input is a defect. Claims c2 (FP32 2/pi boundary rounding) and c3 (cosine polynomial truncation) were cleanly rebutted by t10 and t11, so no other concerns remain.
